newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt unlikely to buy wheat until Dec -official.
newsitem.headline: Egypt unlikely to buy wheat until Dec -official.

text.p: Egypt's expected wheat harvest of 5.9 million tonnes and its large reserves will keep it out of the grain market until at least December, the main official in charge of government commodity purchases said on Wednesday.

Samir Shakankiri, vice-chairman of the General Authority for Supply Commodities (GASC), told Reuters the state would probably buy at least two million tonnes of the 1997 harvest and that amount would cover consumption for about four to 4-1/2 months.
"We have our reserves. We won't need wheat until December and the amount we will buy locally will reduce the pressure on international markets," Shakankiri said.
He did not specify how much Egypt had in reserve but he told Reuters in February, after buying 400,000 tonnes of Australian wheat, he had grain to tide him over until July at least.

Supply and Trade Minister Ahmed Gueily said this week Egypt had grown 5.9 million tonnes of wheat, a figure which is lower than the seven million tonne harvest forecast by Agriculture Minister Youssef Wali late last year.
In the previous season, which ended in the early summer of 1996, the country grew 5.7 million tonnes of wheat, slightly less than it initially hoped.
